statements.markdown: Figure 5: Cross-team collaboration and idea lineage.
statements.note: Figure 5b weights each improvement by log(old cost/new cost), rather than counting records: the log gains add to log(start cost/best cost) within each application. The authors classify gains after both sharing channels were active and average the resulting application shares equally, reporting 15% for wiki or Lean-file sharing and 24% for conferences.

statements.markdown: we classify every verified gain by where its new idea originated
statements.note: In Fig. 5b, a drop from cost $C_i$ to $C_{i+1}$ contributes $\log(C_i/C_{i+1})$. Two successive halvings get equal weight under that measure. The authors compute shares within each application after both channels were in use and average the shares across the three applications.

statements.note: In the stopping-power example in Fig. 5c, Teams 2 and 3 reduced a shared register from $288$ to $231$ ancillas over five wiki records, with conference input from Team 1. The proof certifies the resource count. The attribution also uses the sequence of exchanges recorded by the teams.
